disposition.reason: Python backtest_view.VIEW_SELECT and install_view own the current ordinary QuestDB view definition. Java provides a typed read contract without creating a competing DDL or materialization owner.
disposition.java_surface: Thirteen-field typed READ-only view definition, bounded repository and ReadGroup binding.
disposition.write_rejection: ObjectKind.VIEW and READ-only capability reject direct Java writes.

contract.time_semantics: Exchange business date in an output TIMESTAMP, not a designated physical view timestamp.
contract.is_suspended_type: LONG in the current view; retained physical backtest_daily uses INT.

python_owner.installer: install_view checks unique (date, ts_code) upsert keys on stk_factor, stk_limit and stk_st_daily before CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW.
python_owner.suspension_input: stk_suspend is grouped by timestamp and ts_code before joining; a second branch synthesizes suspended days from previous close.
python_owner.refresh: Ordinary view dynamically reads base tables; no independent refresh job or checkpoint.

target.reason_no_isolated_write_target: An ordinary view has no physical rows or direct writer; Python's current catalog definition was compared in place by SELECT only.

read_acceptance.database_access: Configured local QuestDB through HTTP/QWP and JDBC; SELECT only.

known_limitations: The field comparison covers one real date and its first 200 ordered keys, not the entire historical view.
Java intentionally does not install or replace the Python-owned view; no DDL was executed.
